mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last four weekly means (-9.1, -6.9, -5.1, -3.4), a monotone recovery trend of roughly 1.9 points per week; this momentum persists, so the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -9.1 at t-3w to -3.4 at t-0w with no weekly reversal
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the prior 28-day mean despite four consecutive weekly gains at the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has recovered from -31.9 to -27.7 and retail footfall follows transit use with a short lag; once TRANSIT crosses back above -25 percent of baseline, the additional station traffic translates into higher discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -25 percent of baseline, i.e. at least 2.7 points above the t-0w reading of -27.7.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT gained 4.2 points across the four weekly means
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses above -25 percent, the following 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than its value in the 14 days before the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM rising to +5.7 while RESIDENTIAL slips from +4.0 to +3.1 shows households shifting spend from at-home provisioning toward out-of-home activity; the substitution continues and pushes RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 0.9 points while GROCERY_PHARM rose 3.4 points over the window
regime_hint: steady state with reopening consumption substitution
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL keeps falling while GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising, yet the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS fell 6.4 points week-on-week to -16.4, a sharp outdoor-activity retrenchment that signals a general mobility shock; households cut non-essential trips, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next week relative to the last one.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points week-on-week, as it did from -10.0 at t-1w to -16.4 at t-0w.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -10.0 to -16.4 in the final week
regime_hint: local outbreak response or adverse-weather retrenchment
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS falls more than 5 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC does not fall over the subsequent 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: Any re-imposition of restrictions after 15 December will first cut WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, which are the leading edge of reduced movement; retail footfall then follows downward, so the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC falls below the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls at least 1.5 points week-on-week from the t-0w level of -6.7.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has been flat at -6.7 for two weeks, leaving room for a restriction-driven drop
regime_hint: re-introduction of restrictions following an outbreak
failure_condition: A restriction episode occurs, WORKPLACES falls at least 1.5 points in a week, and the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is still above the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The 28-day window starting 15 December contains the Christmas and Boxing Day shopping peak; holiday spending lifts retail footfall irrespective of the mobility base, so the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean even if other series stay flat.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-12-15 places the Christmas and Boxing Day sales inside the forward 28-day window
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the last 28-day mean, showing no holiday uplift.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT is recovering while WORKPLACES holds flat at -6.7, meaning the mobility recovery is driven by non-commute trips; every additional point of transit recovery adds discretionary footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT gained 4.2 points while WORKPLACES moved only 1.3 points
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues rising while WORKPLACES stays within 1.5 points of -6.7, yet the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM climbed every week to +5.7 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +3, indicating holiday pantry-loading and continued home-stay substitution; the grocery share of household spend crowds out discretionary retail, pushing the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC down.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5.0 for two consecutive weekly readings.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 2.3 to 5.7 over the four weekly means while RESIDENTIAL stayed above 3
regime_hint: holiday stockpiling and pre-cautionary pantry loading
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays above +5.0 for two more weeks and the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is above the prior 28-day mean.
